facts: Two persons Indrajit Kaur and Arjun had filed an appeal questioning their conviction and imposition of sentence.

Each one of them was convicted for offences punishable u/s. 302 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short 'the IPC') and sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs.3,000/with default stipulations.

They were also convicted for the offences punishable u/s. 201 read with S. 34 IPC and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for three years and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/with default stipulations.
The appeal was allowed by the impugned judgment, so far as present respondent is concerned.
issues: Challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Bombay High Court at Aurangabad.
petitioner_arguments: The accusations were established against A-1. The same analogy should have been applied in the case of the present respondent.
respondent_arguments: Supported the judgment of the High Court.
court_reasoning: The circumstances which were pressed into service to fasten the guilt on the accused are, as follows:

So far as the purchase of rat killer poison and the gunny bag is concerned, there was no evidence to show that either the rat killer poison or the gunny bag was purchased prior to the date of occurrence.

The only other circumstance is purported discovery of the dead body at the instance of the respondent. The High Court has found that this so-called discovery on the basis of the information given by A-2 has not been established.
holding: Above being the position, we find that the High Court's judgment does not suffer from any infirmity to warrant interference.
